title: National Rental Affordability Scheme (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2008

speeches.speaker: Nick Sherry
speeches.brief: The speaker moved that the bills be taken together and read a first time without formalities, and the motion was agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Nick Sherry
speeches.brief: The speech announced the introduction of several bills, including education legislation that appropriates over $0.5 billion for Indigenous education programs from 2009 to 2012, and a Schools Assistance Bill providing $28 billion for non-government schools, with a focus on closing Indigenous educational gaps. It also introduced revised heavy vehicle registration charges to end cross-subsidisation, a road user charge increase to 21 cents per litre, and a $70 million Heavy Vehicle Safety and Productivity Package.

speeches.speaker: Marise Payne
speeches.brief: The opposition supports the government's National Rental Affordability Scheme but has reservations and will move amendments, noting a forecast undersupply of 200,000 homes by the next election and that the scheme provides over $600 million for 50,000 affordable rental units with a $6,000 annual tax offset plus $2,000 state top-up.

speeches.speaker: Marise Payne
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the National Rental Affordability Scheme would only address a small fraction of the projected 200,000 housing unit shortfall, and raised concerns that its fixed $6,000 annual incentive and rigid parameters may fail to attract institutional investors or deliver a competitive rate of return. The speaker also noted the scheme's tenant eligibility criteria could exclude key workers and that the government had only provided a temporary two-year fix for the charitable status of not-for-profit participants.

speeches.speaker: Ursula Stephens
speeches.brief: The government argued the National Rental Affordability Scheme, assessed on sustainability and accessibility criteria, would reduce rental stress and increase affordable housing supply. The government opposed parts of Senator Payne's amendment, citing constitutional issues with sliding-scale tax offsets and concerns that a 30% income increase would shift focus to moderate-to-high-income households, while the Greens supported requirements for solar panel rebate access and that 20% of incentives target projects of 20 or more dwellings.

speeches.speaker: Ursula Stephens
speeches.brief: The government moved amendments to the National Rental Affordability Scheme (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2008, extending the definition of 'charitable purpose' so that not-for-profit community housing providers participating in the scheme during its 2008-09 and 2009-10 establishment phase would not risk losing tax concessions. The opposition and the Australian Greens criticised the amendments as a short-term fix that created uncertainty for charities and threatened the scheme's viability, urging a permanent resolution before the third round of allocations.
